saa-ini-085.text: An unexpected marketing campaign will require extra servers for only two weeks, without any long-term commitment, and the load will not tolerate interruptions. EC2 is the appropriate for this punctual need?
options: On-Demand, paying per second of use without obligation
saa-ini-085.explanation: On-Demand is exactly for temporary and unpredictable needs that do not tolerate interruption: you pay the full fee, but only for the period used, without contracts.
saa-ini-085.hint: Short term + no commitment + no interruption: which model charges more dearly for this freedom?
optionRationales: On-Demand is exactly for temporary and unpredictable needs that do not tolerate interruption: you pay the full fee, but only for the period used, without contracts.
Booking for three years to use two weeks would waste almost all the commitment paid.
The price would be lower, but the possibility of interruption with 2 minutes of warning violates the requirement not to tolerate interruptions.
A one-year spending commitment makes no sense to a two-week demand.

saa-ini-086.text: Tax reports are generated monthly and stored in S3. They are frequently consulted in the first month, rarely after 90 days and, by legal requirement, must be retained by 5 which mechanism of S3 automates the movement of these objects to cheaper classes as they age?
options: Lifecycle Policy (Lifecycle Policy) with scheduled transitions between classes
saa-ini-086.explanation: Life cycle policies automate transitions by object age (e.g. for Standard-IA after 90 days, Glacier after) and expiry at the end of retention — cost optimization without manual intervention.
saa-ini-086.hint: Think of the 'automatic treadmill' that takes the object to increasingly cheaper shelves as it ages.
optionRationales: Life cycle policies automate transitions by object age (e.g. for Standard-IA after 90 days, Glacier after) and expiry at the end of retention — cost optimization without manual intervention.
Version preserves versions of objects against accidental changes — does not move objects between storage classes.
A CRR copy objects to another Region (resilience/geographical compliance), without any automatic transition of classes by age.
Transfer Acceleration accelerates long-distance uploads — no relationship to cost management per life cycle.

saa-ini-087.text: A data lake in S3 contains millions of objects whose access patterns change unpredictablely over time. The team cannot define fixed transition rules and wants the same S3 Optimize costs by moving each object to the appropriate access layer, without recovery fees. Which storage class resolves this?
options: S3 Glacier Deep Archive for everything
saa-ini-087.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering monitors the access of each object and automatically moves it between layers (frequency, frequency, archiving), without recovery rates or need for manual rules — ideal for unpredictable patterns.
saa-ini-087.hint: When you don't know the access pattern, delegate the decision to the 'intelligent' class'.
optionRationales: Intelligent-Tiering monitors the access of each object and automatically moves it between layers (frequency, frequency, archiving), without recovery rates or need for manual rules — ideal for unpredictable patterns.
Keeping everything in the most expensive class ignores the economy available to rarely accessed objects — just the waste to eliminate.
File everything would make the recovery of objects still active slow (hours) and expensive — unfeasible for data with unpredictable access.
One Zone-IA reduces resilience (one AZ) and charges recovery rate — bad for objects that are accessed again frequently.

saa-ini-088.text: By regulatory requirement, digitised medical records must be retained by 10 years, but they will almost never be consulted — and, when they do, a wait until 12 hours for recovery is acceptable. What class of S3 offers the MENOR storage cost for this scenario?
saa-ini-088.explanation: Deep Archive is the cheapest class in the whole AWS, designed for long-term retention (7-10+ years) of data almost never accessed, with standard recovery in up to 12 hours — perfect fit for regulatory filing.
saa-ini-088.hint: Decades of retention + half-day patience to recover = the cheapest 'deep dead archive' in the catalog.
optionRationales: Deep Archive is the cheapest class in the whole AWS, designed for long-term retention (7-10+ years) of data almost never accessed, with standard recovery in up to 12 hours — perfect fit for regulatory filing.
Standard is optimized for frequent access and costs often more per GB than deep archiving classes.
The Instant Retrieval offers recovery in milliseconds at a higher cost — unnecessary when 12 waiting hours are acceptable.
Standard-IA meets infrequent accesses that require immediate recovery — more expensive than the Glacier classes for decade-long retention.

saa-ini-089.text: An analysis of use revealed that most instances EC2 of a company uses less than 10% of CPU and memory, because they were provided with 'free for warranty'. The recommended practice of adjusting the type and size of the instances to the real need of the load is called what?
saa-ini-089.explanation: Right-sizing is the continuous process of adapting the type and size of resources to the real demand of the load, eliminating the cost of oversupply without sacrificing performance.
saa-ini-089.hint: The name in English literally means 'righten the size'.
optionRationales: Right-sizing is the continuous process of adapting the type and size of resources to the real demand of the load, eliminating the cost of oversupply without sacrificing performance.
Climbing vertically is AUMENTAR the size of a resource to gain capacity — the scenario requires fine adjustment (usually reduction) to the appropriate size.
Lift-and-shift is a MIGRATION strategy (moving without changing) — not the practice of adjusting the size of resources to actual use.
Load balancing distributes traffic between instances — does not resize over-provided instances.

saa-ini-090.text: FinOps team wants automatic and machine-based recommendations about which instances EC2, volumes EBS and functions Lambda are oversized or undersized, with specific suggestions of more suitable types from the actual metrics of use. AWS generates these recommendations?
saa-ini-090.explanation: Computer Optimizer analyzes historical metrics of machine learning use and recommends ideal types and sizes for EC2, Auto Scaling Groups, EBS and Lambda — the dedicated right-sizing tool of AWS.
saa-ini-090.hint: The name of the service delivers the mission: 'optimize computing' with automatic recommendations.
optionRationales: Computer Optimizer analyzes historical metrics of machine learning use and recommends ideal types and sizes for EC2, Auto Scaling Groups, EBS and Lambda — the dedicated right-sizing tool of AWS.
The calculator estimates planned architecture costs ANTES implementation — it does not analyse the actual use of existing resources.
The CloudWatch collects raw metrics, but does not transform them into sizing recommendations — this is the role of the Optimizer Computer.
The Artifact deliver conformity reports from the AWS — no relationship with optimization of computational resources.

saa-ini-091.text: An electronic commerce site has intense traffic during the day and almost zero at dawn, but keeps the same fixed amount of instances EC2 from the point of view of costs, what architectural change eliminates this waste?
options: Migrate all instances to larger types
Buy Reserved Instances for maximum peak capacity
Configure Auto Scaling to automatically reduce the number of instances in low demand periods
Disable monitoring of CloudWatch to save
saa-ini-091.explanation: The Auto Scaling aligns capacity (and cost) with real demand: less early morning instances, more peaks — paying only for the necessary at every moment.
saa-ini-091.hint: The ideal cost accompanies the demand curve — which mechanism makes the capacity 'breath' together with traffic?
optionRationales: The Auto Scaling aligns capacity (and cost) with real demand: less early morning instances, more peaks — paying only for the necessary at every moment.
Larger instances in fixed quantity would increase the cost — the problem is idle capacity outside peaks, not individual size.
Booking the entire peak guarantees discount, but keeps the waste of the morning paid; reservations make sense for capacity BASE constant.
The monitoring economy would be irritating and blind the operation — without metrics, nor the Auto Scaling Officer.

saa-ini-092.text: Financial manager wants to visually analyze account expenses AWS in the last six months, grouped by service and project tag, identifying growth trends. AWS provides this graphical and interactive analysis of the cost history?
saa-ini-092.explanation: The Cost Explorer is the visual cost analysis tool: interactive graphics with filters and clusters per service, account, tag and period, including trends and forecasts.

optionRationales: The Cost Explorer is the visual cost analysis tool: interactive graphics with filters and clusters per service, account, tag and period, including trends and forecasts.
The Trusted Advisor issues recommendations for good practice (including cost), but is not the graphical exploitation tool of the expense history.
The QuickSight is a generic BI tool for dashboards of any given — the native tool and ready for account costs is the Cost Explorer.
The CloudTrail records calls from API for safety audit — does not show billing analyses.

saa-ini-093.explanation: The AWS Budgets allows you to set custom budgets with alerts on actual or planned spending thresholds, by notifying by email or SNS — the standard budget proactive control mechanism.

The CUR deliver raw and detailed data collection in a pocket S3 for analysis — it does not monitor limits or send alerts.
Computer Optimizer recommends resource sizing — does not accompany budgets or trigger spending notifications.
The Inspector varre security vulnerabilities in workloads — no budget relationship.

saa-ini-094.text: One API internal is used only a few times a day, but rotates in an instance EC2 On 24/7, generating constant cost for very little use. From the point of view of cost optimization, why migrate this API for AWS Lambda with API Gateway would be advantageous?
options: Because Lambda is always cheaper than EC2 in any scenario
Because Lambda does not charge by data transfer
Because in the serverless model you only pay for the real executions, eliminating the cost of idle capacity between calls
Because API Gateway eliminates the need for security and authentication
saa-ini-094.explanation: The Lambda charge by request and duration: no calls, zero cost of computing — for sporadic charges, the economy over an instance 24/7 It's huge..
saa-ini-094.hint: Server connected all day to answer 'from time to time' versus pay only when someone calls — where is the waste?
optionRationales: The Lambda charge by request and duration: no calls, zero cost of computing — for sporadic charges, the economy over an instance 24/7 It's huge..
At loads of very high constant volume, the EC2 (with reservations) can cost less — the advantage of serverless is proportional to the idleness of the load.
Output data transfer continues to be collected normally in serverless architectures.
The API Gateway FACILITA authentication and control, but does not eliminate it — and that is not cost argument.

saa-ini-095.text: A rendering farm processes thousands of animation boards per night. Jobs are fault-tolerant: if one machine is lost, the board simply returns to the queue and is processed by another. What combination of purchase model and justification optimizes the cost of this load to the maximum.?
options: Dedicated Hosts, to ensure maximum performance per server
Spot Instances, taking advantage of even discounts 90% since interruptions do not compromise the jobs
Reserved Instances of 3 years for all rendering knots
On-Demand, because rendering requires the highest possible stability
saa-ini-095.explanation: Discontinuation-tolerant loads are the perfect use case for Spot: the maximum discount of EC2 with operational risk neutralized by reprocessing line design.
saa-ini-095.hint: If you lose a machine 'does not hurt', the idle capacity market pays the biggest discount of EC2.
optionRationales: Discontinuation-tolerant loads are the perfect use case for Spot: the maximum discount of EC2 with operational risk neutralized by reprocessing line design.
Failure tolerance described eliminates the need for guaranteed stability — paying full tariff would waste the main economic opportunity.
Dedicated hosts are the most expensive option and meet licensing/insulation requirements — nothing in the scenario justifies them.
The night demand and yield variable does not justify fixed capacity commitment for three years — reserves meet constant loads.

saa-ini-096.text: The development and approval environments of a company run in instances EC2 and RDS which are only used in commercial hours (8h at 18h, working days), but remain connected all the time. What simple measure can reduce the cost of these environments in up to 70%?
options: Automate the disconnection of the instances outside business hours and reconnect them at the beginning of the file
Buy Reserved Instances of 3 years for test environments
Migrate environments to larger and more modern instances
Replicate environments in a second region to divide the load

optionRationales: Stopped instances do not generate computer cost: turn off dev/approval in ~128 idle weekly hours (nights and weekends) cut most of the cost without affecting the team.
Larger instances would increase the cost — waste is in idle hours, not in the type of instance.
Reservations paid for continuous use 24/7 — for necessary resources only 25% of time, off exceeds the reserve discount.
Duplicate environments DOBRARIA the cost — the opposite of the economy objective.
